description:
## Goal

Verify that all the fixes in this epic actually solve the
crash-after-1-2-days problem. Without a soak test we are
guessing.

## Approach

1. Deploy the fixed binary to the FreeBSD Bastille jail.
2. Use a representative feeds.yml (the production one if it
   is not too big, else a curated subset of ~50 feeds covering
   RSS, Atom, and slow/timeout-prone sources).
3. Run for 48 h. Log RSS every 5 min via the new reporter
   (task 1).
4. Verify at the end:
   - RSS never exceeds 1 GB
   - RSS growth over the last 24 h < 100 MB
   - No OOM kill
   - All expected feeds are still being fetched
5. Capture the qh-snap-* heap snapshots and inspect the
   largest VMAs (anon vs file-backed) to confirm the dominant
   resident set is sane.

## Acceptance

- A report at docs/soak-2026-XX.md with the RSS chart,
  heap snapshot inventory, and a pass/fail verdict.
- If the test fails, the report identifies the dominant
  leak source so we can open a follow-up ticket.

## Note

This task depends on tasks 1-5. Run it last in the epic
sequencing.
title: Long-running FreeBSD 48h soak test with RSS assertions
